newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REDS 1B MORRIS OUT 2-4 WEEKS AFTER SHOULDER SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REDS 1B MORRIS OUT 2-4 WEEKS AFTER SHOULDER SURGERY.

text.p: Cincinnati Reds first baseman Hal Morris underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right shoulder Monday and will be sidelined two to four weeks, the team announced.
Team physician Dr. Timothy Kremchek, who performed the procedure, said Morris should begin rehabilitation Wednesday.

"He had thickness around his labral frame and bursa in his right shoulder," Kremchek said. "We were able to clean it out, which should relieve him of a lot of his pain. He's staying in the hospital tonight."
Morris suffered the injury while diving for a ball May 11 at San Diego. He received a cortisone shot six weeks ago and did not complain of shoulder pain until last week.
Morris should be ready to return to the lineup around September 1, the doctor said.
The 32-year-old Morris is batting .276 with one homer and 33 RBI in 96 games this season. He hit .313 with 16 homers and 80 RBI in 142 games last year.
